claims.statement: Omarchy Gaming System is an API-first social gaming system whose flagship client is a keyboard-first QML connector.

The implemented runtime spans the first-playable social and game system, local operator containment and recovery, the Door Legends provider pilot, and signed marketplace synchronization with independent server-local cartridge admission.
The first playable product outcome requires account and persona creation, social connection, inbox-delivered game challenges, an asynchronous match, and recorded results.
POST /v1/accounts returns only the created account ID and canonical username while validation, conflict, and internal failures use bounded status-specific outcomes.

The device-session API either creates a one-time opaque Bearer token for a password-only account or returns an MFA challenge without creating a session, and its authenticated inventory and revocation remain account-scoped.
Authenticated persona creation, inventory, and editing derive account ownership from a validated device session, while public lookup accepts an exact canonical handle without authentication.
Every persona response is mapped to the seven public profile fields and structurally omits account ownership and authentication material.
Connections, private inboxes, challenges, and game history define the current game-first product; a public message board is only a possible later complement.

A Bearer-authenticated account can enroll, confirm, inspect, and disable optional TOTP MFA, while password login for an enabled account must complete a separate challenge with a TOTP or unused recovery code.

Authenticated social commands owner-scope an acting persona to the Bearer account, expose only public persona profiles, and implement idempotent requests, acceptance, removal, directional private blocking, and unblock.

An accepted persona pair owns one durable private conversation whose participant-scoped API exposes typed server and user messages, monotonic unread state, and history that remains readable after disconnect or block.

Each owned persona has a monotonic retained synchronization cursor: REST is durable recovery truth, while a header-authenticated owner-scoped WebSocket emits only advisory wakeup and resynchronization hints.
The public game catalog deterministically projects exact authority-tagged manifests, and production registers immutable Signal Siege v1 for one human and Signal Siege v2 for exactly two humans.

Authenticated game-session inventory and detail require owned-persona participation and return exact authority, version, revision, lifecycle, bounded state or provider view, completion, ordered public participants, and timestamps from durable storage.

A compiled-game participant command carries a session-wide idempotency UUID and expected revision, executes the stored exact rules version, and returns the committed authority, revision, lifecycle, and state.

ADR-0002 establishes signed data-only Game Cartridges rendered by trusted OmarchyGS QML and now authorizes only the operator-pinned Door Legends v1 remote-authority pilot; compiled Signal Siege remains platform-authoritative.

Production includes the signed cartridge contract, secure staging, trusted Core/Rich-2D rendering, the Door Legends provider pilot, and one pinned marketplace-to-server catalog path; the main client still does not acquire, mount, or launch cartridge packages.

Developers validate cartridge packaging, trusted rendering, deterministic SDK and release import, and the dormant provider security boundary with the four focused cartridge and provider conformance scripts.
An authenticated owned persona can create a retry-safe exact-version challenge only to a connected unblocked peer, and participant-scoped inventory and detail retain pending and terminal history.

Challenge acceptance is reserved for the challenged persona and atomically creates one exact game session, while decline, cancellation, and server-owned expiry create terminal history without a session.

An authenticated account can start an exact one-human game for an owned persona through a durable idempotency receipt, with replay before current registry or active-cap admission and at most 25 active solo starts per persona.

Signal Siege v1 is a deterministic one-human tactical duel whose human and server-owned bot resolve simultaneous strike, guard, or charge rounds and produce a bounded core-destruction or twelve-round outcome.

The keyboard-first QML client can browse the compiled catalog, create and resolve two-person challenges, open exact sessions, submit revision-checked actions, refetch authoritative state, and recover a terminal Signal Siege match through two independent authenticated persona authorities.

The QML game controller retains no bearer credential; it receives a selected-persona request gateway from the bearer-owning onboarding controller and rejects malformed, cross-actor, duplicate-participant, wrong-cardinality, or unsupported compiled-game envelopes before presentation.

The flagship QML shell applies one semantic visual system across all ten routes and the trusted cartridge renderer, with explicit plain-text presentation and focused tests for headings, state, contrast, keyboard traversal, Escape authority, a persistent close control, and 640-by-420 containment.

The accepted long-term deployment unit is an independently owner-operated OmarchyGS community whose standard server owns server-local identity, policy, catalog, and history without implying federation.

Ticket 032 implements one vetted marketplace's server-side synchronization, reviewed inventory, local admission, and authenticated metadata catalog; player acquisition, operator-custom trust, a public Provider SDK, and a general module runtime remain later work.

The flagship QML connector ships as an Arch any-architecture player package with an exact 38-file runtime inventory, relocatable launcher, one Game desktop entry, and non-secret provenance; it depends on qt6-declarative and excludes the Rust server.

Native client artifacts are unsigned private-alpha builds: the documented lifecycle uses a reviewed checkout to build and inspect, pacman to install or upgrade, and pacman removal, while public repository publication, signing, and automatic updates remain unimplemented.
An authenticated owned persona can create a bounded persona-targeted report under a UUID, with exact replay, a 25-open-report cap, and a response limited to the immutable creation receipt.
The QML social flow resolves an exact public handle, retains one report UUID for an exact uncertain retry, validates the minimal receipt, and clears player-entered report fields only after success.

`omarchygs-admin` remains a locally invoked owner tool: database-authorized report, account, invitation, and catalog commands are distinct from guarded HTTPS marketplace synchronization, and no remote administration API is introduced.
Public discovery advertises `games.cartridge-catalog.v1`, while authenticated `GET /v1/cartridges` returns only effective selected marketplace metadata and no acquisition path or executable content.

Marketplace synchronization verifies one canonical signed snapshot, stages exact releases through the existing secure store, and publishes the reviewed inventory only through one atomic PostgreSQL snapshot update.
